entities.summary: Gaius Domitius Dexter was a prominent Roman senator and military commander who served as consul twice, first as suffect consul prior to AD 183, and notably as ordinary consul in AD 196. His career spanned the turbulent reigns of Commodus, the Year of the Five Emperors, and the consolidation of power under Septimius Severus, making him a witness and participant in a crucial transitional period for the Roman Empire. His repeated elevation to the consulship, particularly the prestigious ordinary consulship, underscores his political acumen and the trust placed in him by the reigning emperors, reflecting the shifting loyalties and power dynamics within the Roman elite during the late Antonine and early Severan dynasties. As a member of the ancient and influential *gens Domitia*, his established aristocratic background provided a foundation for his imperial service.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gaius Domitius Dexter's career illustrates the resilience of the Roman administrative system and the role of the senatorial elite in maintaining stability during a period of imperial transition, providing a valuable case study of political survival and service. His high offices, particularly the Urban Prefecture, directly contributed to the functioning of the empire under Septimius Severus.
